name: ams1117_smoke
description: One block on a page of its own: the readability probe for the LDO idiom (task 010). The block now carries hand-drawn geometry — three parts, ten wire runs, one flag per rail — so the assembler replays those wires and flags instead of synthesising an anchor per pin endpoint. It is the same page the 2026-09-18 real-host smoke rendered with synthesised anchors (eight per-pin flags, not one wire, U1's left edge six texts deep), kept as the before/after. What a human has to judge here is whether this reads as a schematic: is the topology legible, does any text sit on another, and does the page look drawn rather than stamped.

provenance.note: Not a product page — a readability probe. It exists so a hand-drawn block can be looked at on a real canvas before more blocks are written on the strength of the rule.

blocks.note: Centred by hand so the drawing has room to be read. The block's own layout is authored on the block's page and is not re-solved here.
